name: Ultraformer III
lead: Ultraformer III is a Korean high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) device used for noninvasive facial lifting and skin rejuvenation. Published studies in the sources cited here mainly concern the related Ultraformer MPT model, and are listed as such below.[2][3]

HIFU is described as a noninvasive approach to facial rejuvenation reported to promote collagen synthesis and reduce subcutaneous fat.[1] Studies have examined its effects by frequency, by facial aesthetic unit using 3D scanning, and on eyelid sagging.[1][2][3]

paras: HIFU delivers focused ultrasound energy to skin layers at selected depths; a 2025 study examined how different frequencies affect specific skin layers and correlated histology with patient-reported outcomes.[1]

A 2024 study of 50 patients used three-dimensional scanning to measure lifting across seven facial aesthetic units after HIFU with Ultraformer MPT.[2] A prospective cohort of 34 Korean women with mild to moderate eyelid laxity received a single HIFU session with Ultraformer MPT and was evaluated for efficacy and safety; its authors note that noticeable improvement in eyelid sagging with noninvasive methods has been challenging.[3] A 2025 histology study compared HIFU frequencies against subjective assessments.[1]

Registered trials include a 273-participant study of a HIFU device for submental and neck laxity, a 180-participant eyebrow-lifting study, and a small trial combining Ultraformer MPT with fractional CO2.[4][5][6]

card.summary: Korean HIFU lifting device; published studies are small and mostly cover the related Ultraformer MPT model.
card.note: Cited studies concern Ultraformer MPT rather than the III specifically.

quick.overview:
Ultraformer III is a Korean HIFU machine used in clinics for non-surgical facial lifting.

Published studies are small cohorts, mostly on the related Ultraformer MPT, covering facial lifting by area, eyelid sagging and ultrasound frequency.
quick.mechanism: Focused ultrasound heats tissue at selected depths, described as promoting collagen synthesis and reducing subcutaneous fat.
quick.risks: Safety details were not available beyond the studies' own safety evaluations; several larger device trials are registered.
